Title: Speech during the G-24 Ministers' Meeting
text: SPEECH BY PRESIDENT ANTONIO CASAS GONZALEZ DURING THE G24 MINISTERS' MEETING In handing over the chairmanship of the Group of Twenty-Four to my Algerian colleagues, I feel obliged to acknowledge all the members of the Group and the observer countries that have actively participated in our meetings and to thank them for their support in the course of this short year, during which we had the opportunity to reap the efforts that our predecessors had been making. Let mehighlight three of them. In the first instance, I would like to refer to the unification of the working mechanisms of the G24: today we have a research program fully coordinated with the activities of the Technical Group, which - in turn - was extended to the entire membership. The result of its debates feeds the position and technical arguments of developing countries in the governing bodies of the Bretton Woods institutions and with this has strengthened and enriched ourcontribution to the analysis of the topics of interest with diagnoses and experiences both at the global and regional levels. Secondly, and in perfect communion with this integration of mechanisms and instances, we have the consensus achieved in the creation of an institutional framework that strengthens the processes and evolution of the Group of Twenty-four. This has been a momentous development. In this regard, we would like to acknowledge the important support obtained from the institutions headed by Mr. Mi chael Camdessus and Mr. James Wolfensohn, in making our Secretariat a reality. We must support it in every way so that our work is ever more forceful and timely. At the same time, the United Nations Development Program (PNUD) responded to our request for support for the objective of strengthening South-South and South-North relations. During this year, we have had the invaluable support of that organization, to which we also want to express our sincere gratitude. It is also noteworthy the collaboration of our Executive Directors in the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, whose participation and support have It allowed the integration of the Group's activities in the different forums in which theposition of the developing countries is manifested. An example of these activities is the advice recently initiated by G-24 consultants at the request of the Group of Nine at the World Bank, as well as the very important contribution to the Caracas Ministerial Meeting of some Executive Directors of the Fund and the Bank. However, I believe that this rapprochement should be further deepened through more frequent contacts and exchanges and permanent mechanisms formalising the participationof the G24 in the G9 working meetings. The result of this integration of the Group's processes leads us to the third of our achievements, and perhaps the most substantial, which has been to transform the reactive nature of the Group by areactive action of the Group by a proactive action with a long-term vision. In this regard, I would like to emphasize two aspects that I believe are of the greatest importance for our future: one, the exchange of proposals with the industrialized countries and, the other, theprinciples adopted by the Group in the recent Caracas Declaration. Finally, it is a great pleasure to recognize the important contributions, both content and otherwise, that we have received from our highly appreciated Aziz Ali Mohammed in the G-24 Office; the identification and support of Gerald Helleiner in the management of the research program, and Sabina Bahtia and Patrick Cirillo for their high level of professionalism and efficiency in the preparation of documents and in the ization of our meetings; contributions that -together- have allowed us an outstanding development of our activities. I would like to inform you that for the next autumn meeting, we will be presenting two publications: the first is a compilation of the G-24communiques since 1986, with their respective analytical index to update the work carried out during that year under the presidency of Argentina; the second is a collection of articles that gathers the opinion of qualified authors on the history and perspectives of the G-24. To my colleagues from Algeria, Sri Lanka and Peru, as well as the rest of our members, I reiterate Venezuela's commitment to fulfill the mandate received at the Caracas meeting to collaborate with the development of the relationship with the G-7 and, likewise, to continue supporting this group in its process of renewal and the exercise of leadership that makes our ideas present, Our vision and our participation in decision-making centers related to international monetary and financial issues.
